title: SGit vaults in 90 seconds
subject: sgit.ai — the SG/Vault page, the sgit home page, and a published vault opened live in SG/App
notes: Shape invented for this spike, not taken from the demo-reel pack. Fields: narration (spoken), caption (on-screen, short, different), shot (how the still is made).

shot.url is a public page. shot.annotate is what gets injected into the page DOM before the screenshot: spot = spotlight rect in viewport fractions [x,y,w,h]; label = a tag placed at [x,y]; blur = a blur rect.
shot.focus is the 9:16 crop region used for the vertical cut, in fractions of the landscape still. Absent = whole frame (letterboxed).
shot.kind clip = a Playwright recordVideo clip is shot as well; the still used in the video is a frame from it, because video-creator only takes images.
shorts lists the scene ids used for the vertical cut, in order.
No keys or tokens live here. The published vault read key is scraped from https://sgit.ai/demos/vaults/ at capture time.
label.at is either viewport fractions [x,y] or 'below' / 'above', which anchors the label to the scene's spotlight rect. Absolute fractions were tried first and landed away from their targets.

Narration was tightened after the first render came out at 128 s: 274 words read as 128.5 s of Kokoro at speed 1.0, so 90 s is about 190 words, not the 12 to 15 scenes at 6 to 8 s the recipe suggested.

Round 2: title/subtitle/author/date and intro/outro were added; s01, s10 and s12 moved from hand-measured rects to element targets, resolved through shadow roots and iframes, after the rects missed at the phone viewport.
s10 keeps a rect per format: the vault app renders inside a sandboxed srcdoc iframe whose document the parent page cannot read, so no element target can be resolved there.

Round 4: the intro was rewritten to preview the video after the first one echoed scene one almost word for word. Landscape stills are cropped to the picture area's own aspect around the spotlight, so the page fills the width.

scenes.narration: This is sgit. Git workflows over folders that are encrypted before anything leaves your machine.
scenes.caption: Encrypted before it leaves

scenes.narration: The server stores ciphertext under opaque identifiers. File names, contents and commit messages never reach it.
scenes.caption: The server sees ciphertext

scenes.narration: Creating a vault is one command.
scenes.caption: One command

scenes.narration: Then you work like git. Status, commit, history, sync, and an agent mode built for machines.
scenes.caption: Work like git

scenes.narration: SG Vault is the same vault in the browser. One encrypted wire format, no wrapper around the command line.
scenes.caption: Same vault, in the browser

scenes.narration: You open a vault by its key, carried in the URL fragment. The fragment is never sent, so the server never sees the key.
scenes.caption: The key never leaves the browser

shot.scrollTo: text:You open a vault by its key

scenes.narration: Three pieces. The sgit command line, the SG Vault browser client, and SG Send, the transfer API that never sees plaintext.
scenes.caption: Three pieces, one wire format

scenes.narration: A vault can contain an app. Sharing the vault link is deploying the app.
scenes.caption: The app is the vault

shot.scrollTo: text:Vault apps: the app is the vault

annotate.spot: el:heading:Vault apps: the app is the vault

scenes.narration: sgit dot ai publishes read keys for its demo vaults on purpose. A read key cannot become write access.
scenes.caption: Read keys, published on purpose

annotate.label: keys blurred for the video, not on the site

scenes.narration: Here is one, opened live. Everything on this page was decrypted in the browser with a published read only key.
scenes.caption: Decrypted in your browser

landscape.label: decrypted in the browser, with a published read key

shorts.label: decrypted in the browser, with a published read key

scenes.narration: Behind the app is the vault itself. Files, history and branches, in the same file browser you get for any vault.
scenes.caption: Files, history, branches

scenes.narration: And the badge says what the key allows. One read, zero writes.
scenes.caption: Read-only by construction

annotate.label: R1 W0: one read key, no write key
